c.tagline: Australia's Red Centre heart: outback ranges, Aboriginal art, and the gateway to Uluru.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and booked through Alice Springs Taxis or the 13cabs app; rideshare such as Uber does not operate in Alice Springs, and there is no public bus to the airport, so pre-booking a taxi, airport shuttle or hire car is essential.

emergency.note: 000 is Australia's emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 112 also works from mobile phones.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: Safety index is the main factor (40/100)

avoid.reason: Elevated alcohol-related and property crime; caution in the CBD after dark

hood_desc: The compact heart of town around the pedestrian Todd Mall, lined with Aboriginal art galleries, cafes, pubs and the weekend market; the walkable base close to museums and tour departures.
A leafy older residential quarter just east of the Todd River, known for its shady streets, local cafes and an easygoing, arty neighbourhood feel.
The southern approach at Heavitree Gap, where the MacDonnell Ranges pinch the road, river and railway together; a handful of resorts and lodges at the literal gateway to town.
A quiet western suburb along Larapinta Drive heading toward the West MacDonnell Ranges, with family homes, budget lodges and easy access to the ranges and Desert Park.
A calm eastern estate built around a championship golf course and the ranges, offering resort-style stays and self-contained apartments away from the town-centre bustle.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though the mineral taste leads some to prefer bottled.

transit.hours: Town buses run roughly 7:30am to 6pm on weekdays with limited Saturday services and little on Sundays; taxis cover the evenings.
transit.note: Alice Springs has a small public bus network (ASBus) covering the town and suburbs; there is no rail commuter or tram service, so most visitors rely on taxis, tour coaches or a hire car to reach the outback attractions.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver or with a prepaid Tap and Ride card; day passes offer better value for a full day of sightseeing.

tip.r: Tipping is not expected in Australia; wages are high and service is included, though rounding up for great service is welcome.

landmarks: The town's defining lookout, where a war memorial obelisk surveys Alice Springs framed by the rugged MacDonnell Ranges at sunrise and sunset.
An acclaimed showcase of Central Australian ecosystems, where dingoes, bilbies, and free-flying birds of prey star against a Red Centre backdrop.
Alice Springs Telegraph Station Historical Reserve
The beautifully preserved 1872 repeater station that gave the town its name, set beside the original 'Alice' waterhole on the Todd River.
Royal Flying Doctor Service Tourist Facility
An engaging museum inside a working RFDS base, telling how flying medics deliver healthcare across an outback area larger than Western Europe.
Alice Springs School of the Air
The 'world's largest classroom', broadcasting lessons to remote outback children since 1951, with a visitor centre overlooking live studio lessons.
Alice's arts heart, combining Albert Namatjira watercolours and Papunya boards in the Araluen Arts Centre with museums of natural history and aviation.
A majestic red-quartzite chasm in the West MacDonnells minutes from town, where black-footed rock wallabies emerge around a permanent waterhole.
An arid-zone botanic garden founded by a pioneering anthropologist, its Annie Meyers Hill lookout offering lovely town views among wallabies and mulga.
A close-encounter menagerie of thorny devils, frill-necked lizards, and 'Terry' the saltwater crocodile, starring the Red Centre's coldest-blooded locals.

train.note: The Ghan transcontinental train calls at Alice Springs on its Adelaide–Darwin run (about 24 hrs south to Adelaide, ~24 hrs north to Darwin); it is a tourist rail journey rather than a commuter service.

bus.note: Greyhound Australia coaches connect Alice Springs with Darwin (~22 hrs north via Tennant Creek and Katherine) and, with connections, the southern states; tour coaches also run to Uluru and Kings Canyon.

ferry.note: Alice Springs is a landlocked desert town with no ferry service.

half.name: Standley Chasm (Angkerle Atwatye)
half.blurb: An 80-metre-high slot canyon that blazes molten orange when the midday sun strikes its sheer walls, sacred to the Western Arrernte people.

full.name: West MacDonnell Ranges (Ormiston & Ellery)
full.blurb: A string of gorges, swimming holes and gaps — Standley Chasm, Ellery Creek, Ormiston Gorge — stretching west along Namatjira Drive.
